content: @Eamon Duede, I think it's probably inappropriate to post your own/close collaborators' papers here with just their abstracts. It's a bit too much like advertising, rather than generating / assisting some interesting discussion.
understood. i've deleted. My intention was not to advertise but to seed a list of general papers about AI / ML + Lean specifically

Since many are doing academic work in this space, it would be nice to have a repository of some kind where people can deposit their work that is specifically for papers that focus on AI + Lean. This stuff all appears on the arXiv, too, of course
I would like to read what people are doing!

I have a repository on AI + Math, which initially intended to record papers for "mathematical discovery" (whatever it means). But I started to add more papers on formalization related papers (with tag ATP), but mostly for papers that formalize "new" results discovered by AI (and some benchmark papers, which is another category).
does this mean we should not post our papers on Lean Zulip?

Sorry, I realise I came down a bit hard on @Eamon Duede here, perhaps inappropriately. My apologies. I would like everyone to feel like they can announce their (relevant, on topic) research papers on Zulip!

But I think some bare minimum discussion (even just "I've just posted this on the arxiv, and I think it is relevant to this community because ...") is needed beyond posting abstracts.
(And in particular I'd be happy to hear discussion about Meno, the second paper Eamon tried to post about above, and hope that I haven't prevented that ever happening.)

I think that this makes a lot of sense @Kim Morrison ! With big communities like this, better to run a tight ship than a loose one. And, I completely agree that my original post had too little context to be of genuine use to the community.

I like the proposed approach. So, how about something like the following that every paper post should include:
a) publication status (is this is pre-print, published, draft?)
b) a plain-language explanation of what the paper actually does. Abstracts are often too rigid for a general community
c) relevance statement (why this is relevant to the community?)
